parts.problem_md:
A sector from a circle of radius $r$ has an internal angle of $θ$ radians, as shown below.

![Diagram of a sector with radius r, central angle θ radians, and the arc forming a part of a circle. Lines are marked to indicate the radius.](assets/001-diagram-of-a-sector-with-radius-r-central-angle-.png)

The perimeter of the sector is 4 units and the area of the sector is $A$ square units.

Show that $A = \frac{8 \\theta }{( 2 + \\theta )^{2}}$.
parts.solution_md:
> *The formula for the length of the arc in radians is *$rθ$

> *Find an expression for the total perimeter and set it equal to 4*

$\begin{gathered} r + r \\theta + r & = 4 \\ 2 r + r \\theta & = 4 \textcircled{1} \end{gathered}$

**[B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> This mark is for any correct perimeter equation that uses 4 and $rθ$.

> *The formula for the area of the arc in radians is *$\frac{1}{2}r^{2}θ$

> *Find an expression for the area *$A$

$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} \\theta \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \textcircled{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Eliminate *$r$*, e.g. make *$r$* the subject of equation 1 by first factorising it out*

$\begin{gathered} r ( 2 + \\theta ) & = 4 \\ r = \frac{4}{2 + \\theta } \end{gathered}$

**[M1]**

> *Then substitute this into equation 2*

$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} ( \frac{4}{2 + \\theta } )^{2} \times \\theta$

> *Simplify*

$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{16}{( 2 + \\theta )^{2}} \times \\theta$

$A = \frac{8 \\theta }{( 2 + \\theta )^{2}}$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The last mark is for showing the steps that get you from the substitution of $r$ into $A$ to the answer given (not for writing out the "show that" answer).

parts.problem_md:
In this question all lengths are in centimetres and all angles are in radians.

![q11-0606-w20-qp-12-additional-maths](assets/002-q11-0606-w20-qp-12-additional-maths.png)

The diagram shows the rectangle $ADEF$, where $AF=DE=r$. The points $B$ and $C$ lie on $AD$ such that $AB=CD=r$ . The curve $BC$ is an arc of the circle, centre $O$, radius $r$ and has a length of $1.5r$.

Show that the perimeter of the shaded region is $(7.5+2\mathrm{sin}0.75)r$ .
parts.solution_md:
> *Since arc length, in radians, is *$rθ$* and we are told that the arc length **BC **is *$1.5r$

> *  *

$\mathrm{Angle}BOC=1.5\mathrm{radians}$

**[1]**

> *Use trigonometry to find an expression for the length **BC **in terms of *$r$*.*

> *  *

$\sin ( 0.75 ) = \frac{bevelled \frac{B C}{2}}{r}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to make *$BC$* the subject.*

$B C = 2 r \times \sin ( 0.75 )$

**[1]**

> *Add together the lengths around the perimeter of the shaded area.*

$2 r + 4 r + 1.5 r + ( 2 r \sin ( 0.75 ) )$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$7.5 r + 2 r \sin ( 0.75 )$

> *Factorise by pulling out a factor of *$r$*.*

$(7.5+2\mathrm{sin}0.75)r$* ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

In this question all lengths are in centimetres and all angles are in radians.

The diagram shows the rectangle A D E F, where A F = D E = r. The points B and C lie on A D such that A B = C D = r. The curve B C is an arc of the circle, centre O, radius r and has a length of 1.5 r.

Angle B O C equals 1.5 radians

Find the area of the shaded region, giving your answer in the form $kr^{2}$, where $k$ is a constant correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the area of the rectangle by adding together the lengths **AB, BC** and **CD**, and multiplying it by **DE**.*

> *  *

$Area ( \text{rectangle} ) = ( r + 2 r \text{sin} 0.75 + r ) \times r$

> *Simplify.*

$= ( 2 r + 2 r \sin 0.75 ) r$

**[1]**

> *Write in terms of *$r^{2}$

$= 2 r^{2} + 2 r^{2} ( \sin 0.75 )
= r^{2} ( 2 + 2 \sin 0.75 )
= 3.36 r^{2}$

> *Find the area of the segment by subtracting the area of triangle **BOC **from the area of the sector.*

> *  *

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} ( \text{sector} ) & = 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} \\theta \\ = 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} ( 1.5 ) \end{gathered}$

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} ( \Delta ) & = 1 \frac{1}{2} a b \sin C \\ = 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} ( \sin 1.5 ) \end{gathered}$

$\text{Area} ( \text{segment} ) = 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} ( 1.5 ) - 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} ( \sin 1.5 )$

> *Factorise by pulling out a factor of *$\frac{1}{2}r^{2}$* and simplify to write in terms of *$r^{2}$

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} ( \text{segment} ) & = 1 \frac{1}{2} r^{2} ( 1.5 - \sin 1.5 ) \\ = 0.251 r^{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract the area of the segment from the area of the rectangle.*

> *  *

$\begin{gathered} \text{Area} ( \text{shaded} ) & = 3.36 r^{2} - 0.251 r^{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$3.11r^{2}$* ***[1]**

equations.alt: bold 3 bold. bold 11 bold italic r to the power of bold 2

parts.problem_md:
![q9-2025-specimen-paper-2-cie-igcse-additional-maths](assets/003-q9-2025-specimen-paper-2-cie-igcse-additional-ma.png)

The diagram shows a rectangle $ABCD$ and an arc $AXB$ of a circle with centre at $O$, the midpoint of $DC$. 
The length of $BC$ is $8\mathrm{cm}$ and the length of $DC$ is $30\mathrm{cm}$. Angle $AOB$ is $θ$ radians.

Find the perimeter of the shape $ADOCBX$.
parts.solution_md:
> *Let's label the radius of the sector as *$r$* and angles *$BOC$* and *$DOC$* as *$α$*. *$DO=OC=\frac{30}{2}=15$* cm*

![cie-spec2-q9](assets/004-cie-spec2-q9.png)

> *We can find *$r$* using Pythagoras theorem*

$r=\sqrt{8^{2}+15^{2}}$

**[1]**

$=17$

> *We can find *$α$* using right-angle trigonometry. *$θ$* is in radians so remember to set your calculator to radians*

$\\alpha = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{8}{15} ) = 0.489957326...$

> *Now find *$θ$* by subtracting *$2α$* from *$π$

$\\theta = \pi - 2 ( 0.489957326... )$

**[1]**

$=2.16167800...$

**[1]**

> *(It's worth saving this result in your calculator as it will be used more than once in this question)*

> *Now find the length of the arc using arc length = *$θr$* (or *$\frac{\\theta }{2 \pi } ( 2 \pi r )$* )*

*arc length = *$2.16167800...\times17$

> *And finally find the perimeter of *$ADOCBX$* by adding the 3 straight lengths to the arc length*

$\begin{gathered} \text{perimeter} & = 8 + 8 + 30 + 2.16167800... \times 17 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} = 82.748560... \end{gathered}$

**Final answer:** ** 82.7 cm (3 s.f.) ****[1]**

D O equals O C equals 30 over 2 equals 15
r equals square root of 8 squared plus 15 squared end root
A D O C B X

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

The diagram shows a rectangle ABCD and an arc AXB of a circle with centre at O, the midpoint of DC. The length of BC is 8 cm and the length of DC is 30 cm. Angle AOB is theta radians.

From part (a):
DO = OC = 30/2 = 15 cm
r = square root of (8^2 + 15^2) = 17 cm
theta = 2.16167800... radians

Find the area of the shape $ADOCBX$.
parts.solution_md:
> *We know from part (a) that *$θ=2.16167800...$

> *Find the area of the sector **OAXB*

$\frac{1}{2}\times17^{2}\times2.16167800...=312.362...$

> *Find the area of the triangle **OBC** (and **OAD**) *

$\frac{1}{2}\times15\times8=60$

> *Add together the area of the sector and the area of the two triangles*

$\begin{gathered} \text{Total} \text{area} & = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times 17^{2} \times 2.16167800... + 60 + 60 \\ = 432.362471... \end{gathered}$

** ****[1]**

> *Round the final answer to at least 3 significant figures*

**Final answer:** **432 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** (3 s.f.) ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
![q12-0606-w20-qp-21-additional-maths](assets/005-q12-0606-w20-qp-21-additional-maths.png)

The diagram shows a shape consisting of two circles of radius 3 cm and 4 cm with centres $A$ and $B$ which are 5 cm apart. The circles intersect at $C$ and $D$ as shown. The lines $AC$ and $BC$ are tangents to the circles, centres $B$ and $A$ respectively. Find the angle $CAB$ in radians.
parts.solution_md:
> *Angle *$ACB$* is a right angle because *$CB$* is a tangent to the circle, and the angle between a tangent and a radius is a right-angle. It is also a Pythagorean triple 3, 4, 5 so we know it must be a right-angled triangle. Angle *$CAB$* can be found by*

$\mathrm{tan}θ=\frac{4}{3}$

**[1]**

> *Using the inverse tan function*

$\\theta = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{4}{3} )$

$θ=0.927$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

The diagram shows a shape consisting of two circles of radius 3 cm and 4 cm with centres A and B which are 5 cm apart. The circles intersect at C and D as shown. The lines AC and BC are tangents to the circles, centres B and A respectively.

Find the perimeter of the whole shape.
parts.solution_md:
> *To find the perimeter, we need to use the formula for arc length, *$l=r\timesθ$*.*

> *Angle *$ABC$* can be found by *

$\mathrm{tan}θ=\frac{3}{4}$

$\\theta = \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{3}{4} ) = 0.6435...$

**[1]**

> *The angle of the larger arc can be found by subtracting angle *$CBD$* from *$2π$

> *Angle *$CBD$* is twice angle *$ABC$*, so*

$θ=2π-2\times0.644=4.995...$

> *The length of the larger arc can be found by *

$4\times4.995=19.98...\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *The angle of the smaller arc can be found by *

$θ=2π-2\times0.927=4.429...$

> *The length of the smaller arc can be found by *

$3\times4.429=13.288...\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *The perimeter is the sum of the two lengths*

$33.3\mathrm{cm}$* ***[1]**

> * *

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

The diagram shows a shape consisting of two circles of radius 3 cm and 4 cm with centres A and B which are 5 cm apart. The circles intersect at C and D as shown. The lines AC and BC are tangents to the circles, centres B and A respectively.

Angle CAB = 0.927 radians (from part a)

Angle ABC = 0.6435... ≈ 0.644 radians (from part b)

Find the area of the whole shape.
parts.solution_md:
> *The area of a sector is given by *$A=\frac{1}{2}r^{2}θ$*. *

> *The area of the larger sector is *

$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times 4^{2} \times ( 2 \mathrm{\pi } - 2 \times 0.644 ) = 39.96... cm^{2}$

> *The area of the smaller sector is*

$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times 3^{2} \times ( 2 \mathrm{\pi } - 2 \times 0.927 ) = 19.93... cm^{2}$

**for either sector correct ****[1]**

> *The area of the right-angled triangle is*

$A=\frac{1}{2}\times4\times3=6\mathrm{cm}^{2}$

**[1]**

> *There are two right-angled triangles (the second being a reflection of the original in the line AB), so finding the sum of the two sectors and the two triangles gives*

$39.96+19.93+6+6$

**[1]**

$71.9\mathrm{cm}^{2}$* ***[1]**

equations.alt: A space equals 1 half space r squared space theta
A thin space equals 1 half space cross times space 4 space cross times space 3 space equals space 6 cm squared
39.96 space plus thin space 19.93 space plus thin space 6 space plus thin space 6
bold 71 bold. bold 9 bold cm to the power of bold 2

parts.problem_md:
In this question all lengths are in centimetres.

![q8-0606-w20-qp-13-additional-maths](assets/006-q8-0606-w20-qp-13-additional-maths.png)

The diagram shows the figure $ABC$. The arc $AB$ is part of a circle, centre $O$, radius $r$, and is of length $1.45r$. The point $O$ lies on the straight line $CB$ such that $CO=0.5r$.

Find, in radians, the angle $AOB$.
parts.solution_md:
> *Arc length *$=r\timesθ$

> *Therefore,*

$\begin{gathered} 1.45 r & = r \times \\theta \\ \\theta = 1.45 \end{gathered}$
